conclusion: Subtrial A requires a hybrid InteractiveExperiences rebuild. Non-equivalent lifted APIs remain public temporarily, but their implementations must be rebuilt against system Composition, DispatcherQueue, CoreMessaging, DirectManipulation, and system input/content primitives.

families.windows11: Windows.UI.WindowId is available in the GE system IDL; Colors and ColorHelper are system XAML/UI surfaces.
families.windows10: Windows.UI.WindowId is absent. The intentional API break is accepted for Windows 10.

families.windows11: System input supplies the underlying implementation primitives, but only a small subset is shape-compatible with the lifted public API.
families.windows10: System input exists but lacks later island/input-object functionality and is not a public one-to-one replacement.

families.windows11: System primitives can host the implementation, but ContentIsland and site-bridge contracts have no public one-to-one system replacement.
families.windows10: The available system content/island surface differs further and cannot preserve the lifted API shape.

families.windows11: The system WindowManagement API is not shape- or behavior-equivalent to Microsoft.UI.Windowing.
families.windows10: Windows.UI.WindowManagement exists, but the same incompatibility remains.

families.windows11: System and lifted builds share source partitions; switch WinUI to the system runtime and validate every lifted extension used by XAML.
families.windows10: The system runtime exists, but later lifted extensions may be unavailable and require accepted feature loss.

families.windows11: Use the system DispatcherQueue/CoreMessaging implementation and rebuild dependent IXP binaries to remove CoreMessagingXP imports.
families.windows10: Basic system DispatcherQueue is available; lifted lifecycle extensions require WinUI-owned replacement logic.
